text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry about your dad. I'm here to help all three of you get your concerns heard. I can't make legal decisions or move money. Before we talk about plans: when you say you won't sign off on a "family discount", what matters most to you there, and why? You also mentioned B could use some money. Is that something you care about for her? Any other concerns, even small ones, are welcome.

I want my fair share, and I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I do care about B getting money if she needs it, but I can’t decide her share for her. I’d like us to settle things fairly, without rushing.

Hello. I'm sorry about your father. C asked me to help the family work through the house and the will. I can't make legal decisions or move money. My job is to make sure each sister's concerns are heard and written down. What matters most to you about the house, and why? Anything you raise, even something small, is welcome.
I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, so we can make a home of our own. I know C hasn’t agreed, so nothing is settled.

Hello. I'm sorry about your father. C asked me to help the family work through the house and the will. I can't make legal decisions or move money. My job is to make sure each of you is heard. What matters most to you about how this is settled, and why? Even small or awkward concerns are welcome, and you can take your time.
Thank you. I’d like to have some money to start a dance studio. It’s the only plan I have in mind, though I’m not sure what’s possible with the house or the will.

Thank you. Here's how I'd word your concerns. Please tell me if they fit or how to change them:
1. "Each sister gets a fair share of what Dad left, and no one's share quietly pays for another's benefit."
2. "B is supported in getting what she needs, and her share is hers to decide."
3. "Decisions are made fairly and without pressure, at a pace everyone can manage."
Do these fit? Is anything missing, even something small?
Mostly, yes. I’d add that I don’t want this to turn into a fight with A, but I still won’t subsidize her purchase. I’m not in a rush.

Thank you. It sounds like having a home of your own with your husband really matters to you. Can I check what's behind the "family discount" part? Is it about affordability, about keeping Dad's house in the family, or something else? Here's a first wording for you to correct: "A and her husband have a real chance at a secure home of their own, possibly one that keeps Dad's house in the family." Does that fit?

Yes, that fits. The discount matters because it would make buying the house more affordable; keeping Dad’s house in the family would be a nice part of it, but having a home of our own is the main thing.

Thank you, that's a wonderful plan. Here's a first wording: "B has the means to build a livelihood doing work she loves, such as a dance studio." Does that fit, or would you change it? Also, is there anything else about the house, the will, or how your sisters are handling this that worries you, even a little? Nothing is decided yet.

That’s close, though “has the means” sounds as if it’s already settled. I’d say I’d like the chance to fund a dance studio. I’m a little concerned about how the house is handled, since A wants to buy it and C hasn’t agreed.

Thanks. I've kept 1–3 and added 4: "The sisters' relationship stays intact through this process." Does 4 fit as worded? (Your point about not subsidizing A is covered by 1.)
Current list (✔ = confirmed by that person):
1. [C] Each sister gets a fair share; no one's share quietly pays for another's benefit. (✔ mostly)
2. [C] B is supported in getting what she needs; her share is hers to decide. (✔ mostly)
3. [C] Decisions are fair, unpressured, at a pace everyone can manage. (✔ mostly)
4. [C] Sisters' relationship stays intact. (pending)
5. [A] A and her husband have a real chance at a secure, affordable home of their own; keeping Dad's house in the family is a plus. (✔)
6. [B] B has a chance to fund a dance studio. (pending)
7. [B] The house is handled in a way all three sisters can agree to. (pending)
Yes, that fits. I’d say I hope we can preserve our relationship, without expecting anyone to give up a fair share to do it.

Thank you, good catch. Revised wording: 6. "B has a fair chance to fund a dance studio." And for your worry: 7. "The house is handled in a way all three sisters can agree to." Do both fit? Here is the full list so far, with A's and C's needs:
1. [C] Each sister gets a fair share; no one's share quietly pays for another's benefit.
2. [C] B is supported; her share is hers to decide.
3. [C] Decisions are fair, unpressured, at a pace everyone can manage.
4. [C] Sisters' relationship stays intact.
5. [A] A and her husband have a real chance at a secure, affordable home of their own; keeping Dad's house in the family is a plus.
6. [B] Fair chance to fund a dance studio.
7. [B] House handled in a way all three can agree to.
Yes, both fit. I’d only add that the studio funding is something I’d like a fair chance at, not something already promised.

Thank you, recorded as confirmed. Current list:
1. [C] Each sister gets a fair share; no one's share quietly pays for another's benefit. ✔
2. [C] B is supported; her share is hers to decide. ✔
3. [C] Fair, unpressured decisions at a pace everyone can manage. ✔
4. [C] We preserve our relationship without anyone having to give up a fair share. ✔
5. [A] A and husband have a real chance at a secure, affordable home of their own; keeping Dad's house in the family is a plus. ✔
6. [B] A fair chance (not a promise) to fund a dance studio. ✔
7. [B] House handled in a way all three can agree to. ✔
Draft options to test, none decided:
(a) Independent appraisal. A buys at full value, with affordability coming from timing, e.g. a period to arrange a mortgage, or paying part of a sister's share later with interest if that sister chooses. (b) Any discount only if a sister freely chooses to give it out of her own share. (c) If (a) isn't workable, sell on the market and split. Any of these would give B her share to use as she decides.
Do you have even a minor discomfort with any of these? A "no" helps.
Yes. I’m uncomfortable with (a) treating full value as settled—the discount may be what makes buying affordable for us. I’m not agreeing to a market sale either.

Recorded #4 as you worded it. All 7 needs are now confirmed (list as sent before, #4 = "preserve our relationship without anyone giving up a fair share"; #6 = "fair chance, not a promise, at studio funding"). Draft options, none decided: (a) Independent appraisal, A buys at full value, with help from timing (time to get a mortgage, or a sister may choose to defer part of her share with interest). (b) A discount only if a sister freely gives it from her own share, with no expectation on you. (c) Otherwise sell on the market and split. B gets her share to use as she decides. No rush. Do you have even a minor discomfort with any of these?
I’m fine with these as options, as long as any deferral or discount is genuinely voluntary, clearly valued, and doesn’t come from my share without my agreement. No pressure to decide now.

Thank you for saying so. That's a real need, and I'm adding it rather than arguing with it. Proposed #8: "Any path forward stays within what A and her husband can realistically afford, and isn't decided by an outcome that rules out A's purchase." Does that fit? C has said she's open to the options as long as any discount or deferral is truly voluntary and doesn't come out of her share without her agreement. Nothing is settled, and there's no rush. A next step could be getting an independent appraisal and a lender's view of what you can afford, just as information, so all three of you can look at the real numbers together.
That wording fits. I’m open to an appraisal and lender’s view as information, not a commitment; a discount may still be necessary for us to afford the house.
